assumptions.original: T is a nonnegative horizon. The sample space carries a measure and the filtration is indexed by nonnegative time. The initial value is strongly measurable for the time-zero sigma algebra. The drift is strongly progressive, and almost every drift section is integrable against the horizon time measure.
assumptions.reconstructed: x is strongly measurable with respect to F_0. b is strongly progressive for F. For mu-a.e. omega, b(·,omega) is integrable against lambda_T. No positivity assumption on T.
assumptions.evidence: Full-module binder and definition audit: hx is explicitly StronglyMeasurable[filtration 0]. hEq is proved without hbi, so the fixed-horizon identity remains all-sample under totalized integral semantics. hbi is used only for the path continuity/BV branch.

conclusion.original: Let the scalar initial value be strongly measurable at time zero and the scalar drift be strongly progressive. Suppose its time section is integrable on the horizon almost surely. The initial value plus the drift integral is strongly progressive and has almost surely continuous finite-variation paths on the horizon. At every sample and time in the horizon it equals the initialized primitive computed with the fixed horizon measure. Formula: A_t=x+\int_{[0,t]}b(s)\,ds=x+P_b(t),\quad 0\le t\le T.
conclusion.reconstructed: Define A(t,omega)=x(omega)+∫ b(s,omega) d lambda_t(s). Then A is strongly progressive for F. For every t≤T and every omega, A(t,omega)=x(omega)+∫ 1_{s<min(t,T)}b(s,omega) d lambda_T(s). For mu-a.e. omega, A(·,omega) is continuous and of bounded variation on [0,T].
